Issued at 305 PM EDT Thu Oct 15 2026

Low level warm/moist advection is increasing this afternoon as a 
mid/upper ridge axis shifts across the eastern Great Lakes. Low 
level flow will continue to strengthen over the next several hours 
with some pockets of better low level moisture convergence 
associated with speed convergence overspreads the area. Surface
low pressure across NE Missouri will deepen some as a pair of 
upper level short waves advance east from central CONUS. The 
first of these waves is across the Central Plains this afternoon
and will rapidly get ingested northeast into stronger west-
southwest flow downstream of a more potent/dynamic upper level 
trough currently digging across the Dakotas. 

This evolution still looks inline to support a rapidly 
northward lifting warm front through this evening with a sharp 
increase in low level moisture and northward shift of pool of 
better instability from southeast MO into southern IN/western 
KY. It still appears as though locations in local area south of 
US Route 24 will have a brief window of weak MLCAPES (100-300 
J/kg) in the 01Z-05Z timeframe tonight. Some weak prefrontal 
trough forcing may contribute to more scattered convection after
initial bands of rain showers later this afternoon/early 
evening, with an environment potentially with some near sfc 
based instability to work with. While instability magnitudes 
will remain quite weak, robust low level and deep layer shear 
profiles will build in from the southwest, so will still have to
be watching for some isolated strong-severe potential mid-late 
evening and possibly into early overnight for areas south of 
US-24. The more favorable combination of CAPE/shear still looks 
to be displaced south from southern IL to central IN where some 
isolated tornado potential cannot be ruled out given low level 
shear profiles. Confidence in severe weather potential as far 
north as local area remains on the low side, but will continue 
to monitor far southern locations later this evening/early 
overnight. A good deal of cloud cover/limited instability and 
stronger forcing displaced west and northwest of local area may 
be limiting factors for isolated severe threat.

Sfc low pressure will continue to deepen Friday morning across 
far SE Ontario/Quebec as the more potent northern Plains trough 
approaches the western Great Lakes. Low level height gradient, 
while strong on Friday, does not look as strong as several 
forecast cycles ago as a secondary west-east low level trough 
axis will be dropping into the region Friday afternoon. Wind 
gusts of 25 to 35 mph will look reasonable for most of the area 
with an exception of potential 40+ mph gusts closer to Lake 
Michigan shoreline. A Wind Advisory has been issued for Berrien
MI and LaPorte IN Counties for Friday 18Z to Saturday 03Z. The 
potential strongest winds look to be in the 18Z-00Z period 
following secondary trough passage, with warm lake waters 
helping post-frontal mixing. After 00Z confidence in stronger 
wind gusts begins to diminish somewhat as some thermal 
modification of mass fields could lead to weak lake aggregate 
trough and a slackening of the gradient. This process should 
prolong the potential of lake effect rain showers into Friday 
night across NW IN and perhaps far SW Lower MI.

The strong negative upper height anomaly will be progressive through 
the region with expansive longwave upper ridge spreading across 
central CONUS Saturday. A few nights of frost potential still look 
on track. On Friday night there could be an area across central 
portions of the forecast area that may be situated between 
lingering lake effect clouds to the west, and lingering better 
mixing to the east to allow for some patchy frost. Saturday 
night/Sunday AM will also feature patchy frost potential, with 
best chances across approx SE 2/3rd of the area as weak return 
southwest flow develops across western/southern Great Lakes.

Much of next work week looks much quieter weather-wise as 
primary storm track remains across southern Canada while 
longwave ridging dominates central part of the country. 
Confidence is high in gradual warm up to above normal levels 
during the early to middle portions of next week.
